module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
public import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- `temp_v G v = deg(v)/(n(G) - deg(v))`. -/
noncomputable def temp_v (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : α) : ℝ :=
  let n := Fintype.card α
  let deg := G.degree v
  if n = deg then 0 else (deg : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - (deg : ℝ))

/-- Maximum of `temp_v` over all vertices. -/
noncomputable def MaxTemp (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty α] : ℝ :=
  let temps := Finset.univ.image (temp_v G)
  temps.max' (Finset.image_nonempty.mpr Finset.univ_nonempty)

end SimpleGraph

reformulations.difference: Lean includes an explicit `if n = deg then 0` branch, whereas the source gives the unguarded formula deg(v)/(n(G) - deg(v)).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every vertex of a finite simple graph, Mathlib's degree_lt_card_verts proves deg(v) < n(G). Consequently the guard is always false and the real denominator is strictly positive. The definition therefore equals the source formula on every permitted input. Both the equality and an explicit equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The Lean use site requires a nontrivial vertex type, while the source states the bound for simple connected graphs without explicitly excluding singleton graphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Connectedness excludes the empty vertex type. On a singleton, every degree and vertex temperature is zero, hence MaxTemp is zero. The inequality reduces to 0 ≤ Ls G, which follows from the nonnegative leaf counts defining Ls. Thus the excluded singleton case is automatic. The equivalence between the unrestricted connected-graph statement and its Nontrivial-restricted version was proved for every nonempty finite vertex type in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked both declarations and all uses; GraphConjecture3 is the only problem-file user. Proved that MaxTemp is the attained greatest vertex temperature and equals Δ/(n−Δ), with Δ Mathlib's maxDegree. Tested empty-type restrictions, singleton and edgeless graphs, K₂, K₄, a four-vertex star, and an edge plus an isolated vertex. The scratch proofs compile without errors or sorry dependencies. No duplicate temperature notion was found in Mathlib. The source's displayed all/resolved entries mark Conjecture 3 true and give Pepper's 2004 proof, agreeing with `research solved`; the older JavaScript conjecture array has a stale O flag.
